page_objective: Define accessibility requirements for SIPANEL digital interfaces, content, technical diagrams, forms, navigation, multilingual layouts, and interactive components.

accessibility_philosophy.statement: SIPANEL interfaces must remain clear, readable, usable, and technically accessible for all users across industrial, mobile, desktop, and multilingual contexts.

compliance_target.minimum_requirement: WCAG AA compliance across all public-facing digital interfaces

rules: Do not use low-contrast gray text.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate meaning.
Use orange primarily for emphasis, actions, and focus states.
Ensure dark sections maintain strong readability.
Body text should remain readable on mobile and desktop.
Avoid very small technical labels.
Maintain sufficient line height.
Use clear heading hierarchy.
Avoid dense uninterrupted paragraphs.
All interactive elements must be keyboard accessible.
Tab order must follow visual reading order.
Focus states must be visible.
Modals must trap focus while open.
Users must be able to close overlays with keyboard controls.
Focus indicators must be visible on light and dark backgrounds.
Do not remove browser focus outlines without replacing them.
Focus states must not rely only on subtle color changes.
Use semantic HTML wherever possible.
Provide meaningful alt text for images.
Use aria-labels for icon-only buttons.
Mark decorative icons as aria-hidden.
Use proper form labels and error descriptions.
Announce dynamic content changes when necessary.

alt_text_rules: Project photos must describe the project context.
Technical diagrams must describe the engineering purpose.
Decorative images should use empty alt text.
Avoid embedding critical text inside images without accessible alternatives.
video_rules: Provide captions when speech is used.
Avoid flashing or rapidly changing visuals.

rules: Provide text summaries for technical diagrams.
Use readable annotations.
Allow fullscreen viewing and zoom.
Avoid tiny labels in preview mode.
Do not use color alone to identify technical risk points.
Every input must have a visible label.
Required fields must be clearly identified.
Validation errors must explain the issue clearly.
Do not rely on placeholder text as labels.
Input focus states must be visible.
Error messages must be connected to fields programmatically.
mobile_rules: Use proper input types for phone, email, and file upload.

rules: Avoid tightly grouped controls.
Keep sticky CTAs accessible without blocking content.
Support one-handed mobile use.
Avoid hover-only behavior.
Respect user reduced-motion preferences.
Disable decorative motion when reduced motion is enabled.
Avoid scroll-jacking.
Avoid motion that interrupts technical reading.
Keep interaction feedback available without animation.
Set correct HTML lang attribute.
Set correct HTML dir attribute for RTL languages.
Mirror directional icons for RTL.
Preserve reading order across translations.
Ensure translated text does not break layout.
Navigation landmarks must be semantic.
Mobile menus must be keyboard accessible.
Menu state must be announced to assistive technologies.
Skip links should be available for main content.
Current page or active section should be clearly indicated.
Use table headers correctly.
Provide captions or summaries for complex data.
Avoid image-based tables.
Ensure horizontal scrolling tables remain usable on mobile.
Keep technical data readable and structured.
Use plain technical language where possible.
Explain technical terms when necessary.
Use headings, bullets, and short sections.
Avoid overly dense technical paragraphs.
Provide context before technical detail.

forbidden_accessibility_patterns: Text embedded inside images without alternatives
accessibility_qa_checklist: All text meets WCAG AA contrast.
All images have appropriate alt text.
All mobile touch targets meet minimum size.
All RTL layouts preserve reading order.
implementation_notes: Accessibility must be treated as a production requirement, not an optional enhancement.
All SIPANEL interfaces should be tested with keyboard navigation, screen readers, mobile devices, and RTL layouts.
Technical clarity and accessibility must work together across all brand and website experiences.
